description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after research (prototype proto192.diff) and a cold review
(BLOCK unless one more hunk lands in the same commit; with it, approve).
Base 8de517a28.

THE DEFINITION: a witness is the ARGUMENT -- not narrowed, not restated, not
projected. The only readers of overlapping_witnesses/match_witness's output
are inside instantiate_match (the emptiness early-exit, the per-position
collection + cleaner, the structural gate witness ⊆ σ(P)), and every one
asks what the call SUPPLIED. The pattern-derived witness was wrong both ways:
it wrote unbound pattern variables back in (erasing `binary` in (a,b)->b vs
(binary,int)->int -- why fz-kdt.184 and fz-kdt.120 each needed a second walk
over the raw arguments), and it replaced the argument with the pattern where
the pattern was ground ({int, a} observing {int|binary, binary} reports
{int, binary}, so the gate compared σ(P) ⊆ σ(P) and passed VACUOUSLY: base
answers Known params=[{int, binary}] -- an unsound accept that
refine_contract_inputs then narrows on = D4). "Narrowed by the pattern's
ground parts" MUST NOT be allowed (it re-opens D4). instantiate_match(params,
result, bounds, args): one walk over (params, args). GOES AWAY:
Types::overlapping_witnesses (arity check moves to match_arrow; the emptiness
early-exit becomes the named line `is_empty(arg) → Invalid`, honest at the
clause level), Types::match_witness, one of two collector walks per position
(collect_match_subst node visits 271,779 → 143,684, −47%), the witnesses
parameter, the doc sentences.

THE FOUR HUNKS, ONE COMMIT:
1. The definition above. Red-first: the two D4 gates ({int, a} at {int|
   binary, binary} and its list form: Known → Invalid at base).
2. The D1 FOLD (mandatory): drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings asks
   collect_match_subst at the [] node instead of collect_instantiation_subst
   (HEAD restated [] as [none], a list WITH an element the pure-shape cleaner
   could descend; the raw [] has no element and the cleaner goes blind).
   Without it 192 has 22 verdict regressions -- every `[a]` observing `[]`
   becomes Known [none] -- and a canon mover. Pin X4B/X7 so the invariant is
   asserted.
3. THE COVERAGE FIX (the review's block): FunctionContract::apply's
   arrow_set_covers (contract.rs:197) SKIPS every clause domain that still
   carries a variable (:207), so after hunk 1 a polymorphic clause set can
   never rescue a row and a legal program dies: fx/c1c.fz -- `@spec
   pick({integer, a}) :: a` + `@spec pick({binary, a}) :: a` called with
   {binary, int} | {int, int} prints 7 at base and error[spec/violation]
   under 192 alone. HEAD's restatement WAS "narrow into the clause domain";
   the one-level-up coverage must read a var-carrying clause domain at `any`
   (instantiate its free vars, Types::free_var_ids mod.rs:1517, to any)
   instead of skipping it -- three lines. Measured with it: c1c prints 7,
   C1 satisfied, C3 (a `none` argument at a polymorphic spec) satisfied = C4,
   corpus 0/0/0, lib 1653/0/5, matrix 485/0/9. Red-first: fx/c1c.fz on
   three doors + unit C1/C3.
4. Docs: addressed-arrow.md (~:208 asserts only the two-parameter veto
   scope; the one-tuple-parameter form `{[a],[a]}` at `{[], [int]}` now
   answers Underconstrained where `([a],[a])` at `([], [int])` answers Known
   [int] -- D3 made observable; say so), specs.md:35-42 (coverage reads
   var-carrying domains at any), arrow_match.rs docs.

PINS (37 A/R constructions + 3 gates + probes promoted as named tests
asserting the base verdicts, 4 moving): R2 union-of-arrows → Invalid (base
unsound; reached WITHOUT polarity machinery -- so fz-kdt.184's "promote R2 as
the gate's red-first witness" is subsumed here); R20 Known [int] →
Underconstrained -- pin it HONESTLY as a precision loss that disagrees with
its two-parameter sibling (D3), not as "consistency"; the two D4 gates. X4
`{:done,a}|{:halted,a}|{:suspended,a,()->any}` at {:done, []}: Underconstrained →
Known [] is a DEFECT (the cleaner's max_tuple_arity skip, D2) -- pin as
known-defect with the mechanism named; optional hunk: descend mixed-arity
tuple unions via tuple_positive_alternatives, which closes D2.

MEASURED: interp 0 / run 0 / canon 0 movers; executables 5297; return any
465; FIFO/LIFO canon movers 2 at base AND at 192 (00277, dead_closure --
the research's "0" was wrong; 192 neither adds nor removes schedule
dependence); match_arrow verdicts base 37,936 / K 21,039 / U 2,951 /
I 13,946; 5 callsite rows change verdict (3× Range.reduce_while_cont 6th arg
Invalid → Known: a false negative gone but Known from a non-ground
observation -- pre-existing, fz-kdt.197; the X4 and X6 rows above);
FunctionContract::apply fallback-not-covered 508 → 497 with ZERO rows ever
rescued through a var-carrying clause (why c1c has no corpus witness);
lib 1653/0/5 (base 1613); red-first confirmed (base + the three public_trace
re-pins = 1 failure; the re-pins are falls: activations 258 → 256,
evaluations 890 → 884, zero-change flat at 8). 184 RE-CUT on 192: +247/−47
(arrow_match +178/−37, mod.rs +69/−10), the 13 pin literals 184 updates,
R5/R20 hold, corpus 0/0/0; 184's fix 2 ("never record an upper bound of
none") is INERT on 192 (ablation identical) and is struck there.

BLOCKED BY fz-kdt.198 (the brand model: 192 makes a branded argument's rejection at
a ground int spec position reachable -- decide before landing). BLOCKS
fz-kdt.184. Sequence: 192 → 184 → 183 → 120.

comments.text: PROMOTED TO THE HEAD OF THE CONFLUENCE CHAIN by the fz-kdt.184 cold review (2026-09-03): land this FIRST (192 -> 184 -> 124 -> 183 -> 120). Scope confirmed by measurement: 184's prototype pays for this defect with instantiate_match(params, result, bounds, witnesses, args) -- two full walks per position of which position.upper and observed.lower are discarded and the args walk's MatchWitness is dropped without a `let _`; 120's prototype pays with open_vars(params, args). With witnesses as OBSERVATIONS (the argument, narrowed by the pattern's ground parts, never a restated pattern) one walk over (params, args) yields lower bounds, upper bounds and openness. Reproducer stays: match_arrow([[a], b, (a,b)->b], b, {}, [[int], int, (binary,int)->int]) hands the third witness back as (a,int)->int. Acceptance: 0 corpus movers (interp/run/canon), the R-series and A-series verdict tables from the 184 review unchanged at HEAD (they are the pins), and a test that the witness of a pattern position carrying an unbound variable is the raw argument.

title: A witness is the raw argument: overlapping_witnesses and match_witness go, the structural gate compares what the call supplied, and arrow-set coverage reads polymorphic clause domains at any
